Converged Route A magnitudes for catalogs v4.1 and v5.1

Decision D-B091 (PI, 2026-11-25 10:24). Branch analysis/mag-converged; large outputs in /wd1/mdenolle_data/magnitude_converged. Only the phase19 solver changed: amplitudes, SNR cut, station epochs, the Hutton-Boore distance term, the 150 km pick selection, the 4-MAD rejection, the ComCat ML anchors, the Mw switch at 4.5 and the Mw_cal rule are those of the stored runs.

Independent verification. A separate verifier re-derived the converged magnitudes (scripts and outputs in /wd1/mdenolle_data/magnitude_converged/verify/) and found them fit to replace the paper's magnitudes. Its checks: the solution is the true minimum, it is set by the data and not by the damping (damping 1e-4 changes ML by at most 0.001, damping 1e-2 by 0.026 at the 99th percentile), and the anchor test is not circular (offset from half of the anchors, gap measured on the other half: offshore +0.116 stored, +0.009 converged, in 99.8% of 500 splits closer to zero). Its must-fix items are resolved here: one gauge row with a null-direction check (section 1b); the text that said two gauge rows fix the P-S difference is corrected; the isolated term no longer appears in the station-term tables.
Summary.
  • The phase19 inversion is now solved exactly: the 161,093 event terms are eliminated and the 1,337 station-phase terms come from a direct solve of their Schur complement, followed by two refinement steps. The last refinement step is at most 6e-14 and the relative normal-equation residual at most 3e-13. Two independent solvers agree with it: a sparse LU factorisation of the full normal equations (5e-7) and a column-scaled LSQR, which converges in about 250 iterations to the same output file. One and twelve BLAS threads give the same ML to 6e-15.
  • The stored solver, LSQR stopped at 3000 iterations, is 0.07 from the minimum for the median event and 0.66 at the 99th percentile. It is not reproducible: 1 and 12 threads differ by up to 0.86 (99th percentile 0.075), and a rerun at 12 threads differs from the stored v4.1 file by up to 0.60.
  • v4.1 (the paper), converged minus stored ML, near events (median by region): Blanco -0.67, JdF ridge/plate -0.29, Gorda -0.19, Mendocino -0.19, offshore forearc -0.19, Endeavour +0.06, Explorer +0.01, Axial +0.07, onshore +0.005 to +0.014. v5.1 near events: Blanco -0.70, JdF -0.51, Gorda and Mendocino -0.29, offshore forearc -0.28, Explorer -0.08, Axial -0.06, onshore +0.01 to +0.015 (the D-B091 numbers); v5.1 moves more than v4.1 because its stored run had stopped further from the minimum. The 3,500 'mapped' events (recorded only beyond 150 km) drop by 0.2-0.45 everywhere, onshore included, because the Theil-Sen line that maps them is refitted to the new near ML.
  • With both catalogs converged, v5.1 minus v4.1 is +0.001 (stored pair +0.047) and -0.004 offshore (stored +0.070). The +0.07 offshore shift reported in the v5.1 magnitude piece was a solver artefact; only Axial keeps a real change (-0.24, from the relocation).
  • External references, v4.1: ComCat ML anchor gap at offshore and coastal labels +0.12 -> +0.01; anchor scatter 0.211 -> 0.174; tensor Mw 3-4.5 at offshore labels, near events, ML - Mw +0.11 -> -0.07 (v5.1 +0.26 -> -0.02). The ComCat ML anchors favour the converged solution clearly; the tensor comparison does not decide between the two (43 events, overlapping 95% intervals, Gorda worse, section 4).
  • 'Onshore' is not uniform: near events at onshore labels south of 42 N (northern California, 4,527 events in v4.1, 3,708 of them labelled 'Other onshore') drop by -0.18 to -0.19 with the northern California network NC; north of 42 N they change by +0.01. The onshore Mc box b goes from 0.92 to 1.01.
  • Gauge rows (verifier must-fix): the stored design had two gauge rows, of which the S row was absorbed by one isolated term (7D.J35C@2013-08-09|S, C = -303). Now the isolated picks are dropped, one gauge row is used, and the solver checks that the gauge rows equal the null directions. ML is unchanged (largest difference 0.0015 in the design test, see section 1b for the full-chain comparison).
  • Gauge: every ocean-bottom deployment is tied to the land network well enough that its formal level error is below 0.1 (most below 0.03); a bootstrap gives errors 1.0-1.7 times larger (NV 2014 about 0.12), and the thinly tied ones carry about 0.1 of model uncertainty. The stored offsets came from the solver, not from weak ties. The ties that are thin are NV 2014, 7A 2010, NV 2011 and OO 2014 (Axial). X9 (Blanco) has only 3-4 events with land picks; 3,800 events shared with 7D Y2, 401 with 7D Y3 and 108 with Z5 2013 carry its level. In phase19 the anchors set one global offset only; the cross-links set every deployment level. The northern California land network NC also moved, by +0.15 against the other land networks (v4.1). That is why Mendocino changes by -0.19 in every year, 2010-2011 included.
  • Mc (paper method, v4_mc_maps.py on v4.1): Blanco 2.2 -> 1.6, Gorda 2.1 -> 1.9, Mendocino triple junction 1.7 -> 1.5, Endeavour-Explorer 1.8 -> 1.6, offshore pooled 2.2 -> 1.7; onshore unchanged. The Blanco Mc 'improvement' between 2011-2012 and 2013-2015 (2.6 -> 2.2) disappears (1.5 -> 1.6), and the Blanco M >= 2.5 rate of 2010 and 2016 relative to 2013-2015 rises from 5% and 8% to 28% and 29%. The paper's Fig. 2, Figs. S3-S7, Table S6, the clustering (Figs. 5-6, Table S5) and about 30 numbers change (list in the last section).

1. Solver change and convergence proof

phase19 fits station ML = M_i + C_jp to the Hutton-Boore station magnitudes within 150 km, with damping 1e-3 and gauge rows of weight 1000 (section 1b for the gauge). The stored runs solved it with LSQR stopped at 3000 iterations (istop 7). LSQR is slow on this system for two reasons. First, the column norms range from 1 (an event with one pick) to 130 (a station-phase term with 16,876 picks), and the gauge rows have weight 1000. Second, moving a whole deployment against its events changes the misfit little per unknown: the eigenvalue of that mode is the deployment's stiffness divided by its number of terms plus events (X9 0.25, Z5 2013 0.48, OO 2014 0.009, against 1.5e4 at the top of the data spectrum). Starting from zero station terms, LSQR resolves these modes last. Until it does, the large site terms of sediment-covered ocean-bottom stations stay in the event terms, so offshore ML comes out too high.

The new default, phase19_solver.solve(method='exact'), eliminates the event terms (their block of the normal equations is diagonal). The 1,337 x 1,337 Schur complement of the station terms is solved by a symmetric eigendecomposition, and two refinement steps follow on the full sparse system. It raises NotConverged unless the last refinement step is below 1e-8 and the relative normal-equation residual is below 1e-10, or unless the gauge rows equal the null directions (section 1b). --solver lsqr runs a column-scaled LSQR with atol = btol = 1e-12 and fails unless istop is 1 or 2. --solver legacy3000 reproduces the stored runs.

With the phase19 tolerances LSQR reaches istop 2 after 4,600 iterations and is then still 0.064 from the minimum at the 99th percentile (largest 0.14). istop 2 bounds the gradient, not the error: in a soft direction the error is the gradient divided by a small eigenvalue. The D-B091 check (4,863 iterations on the stored v5.1 pick set) was therefore close, but not exact (section 4).

The same tolerances on the new one-row system stop with istop 2 after 3,097 iterations, 0.22 from the minimum at the 99th percentile: the stopping test is the problem, not the gauge. The column-scaled LSQR reaches the minimum to 1e-8 in a few hundred iterations.

1b. Gauge rows and null directions (verifier must-fix 1)

The data fix every M_i + C_jp but not a common shift: on each connected piece of the event / station-phase graph, all event terms +delta and all station terms -delta leave the misfit unchanged. The gauge needs one row per such null direction; any further row constrains the fit. The stored runs, and the first version of this work, used two rows (sum of the P terms = 0, sum of the S terms = 0). The graph had two pieces: the main network and one isolated S term, 7D.J35C@2013-08-09|S (9 picks on 9 one-pick events). The S row was absorbed by that term, which ended at C = -303 (v4.1) and -295 (v5.1); stored legacy runs -255 and -234. The two rows therefore fixed the two null directions, and the P - S level difference of the main network stayed free (mean S term - mean P term +0.454). The earlier text of this report said that the two rows fix the P - S difference; that was wrong. Without the isolated term, though, the two rows would have forced mean S = mean P: the misfit rises by about 2,900 and regional ML moves by up to -0.22. The convergence test of the solver does not see this, because the constrained problem is solved exactly too.

Fix: picks not linked to the main network are dropped before each pass (main_component(); their events have fewer than 3 picks, so no ML is lost). ONE gauge row is used (sum of the P terms = 0, which keeps the P terms and the main-network S terms of the previous solution). check_gauge() counts the null directions from the graph (connected pieces) and numerically (eigenvalues of the reduced system below 1e-9 of the largest). It raises NotConverged unless both equal the number of gauge rows and the gauge rows are not orthogonal to the null space. The anchor offset absorbs any single gauge row, so ML does not depend on which one is chosen. The isolated term no longer appears in the converged station-term tables. The stored phase19_station_terms_v51.csv still lists it (C about -234); that value is a gauge artefact and should be ignored.

2. The gauge: how each ocean-bottom deployment is tied to the land network

Groups: every seafloor station-epoch, grouped by network and deployment year (7D = Cascadia Initiative years Y1-Y4); everything on land is the reference. Per group, on the final pick set of the converged run: n_events_with_land = events with picks on the group and on land stations; n_events_with_other_obs = events shared with another ocean-bottom group; n_anchors = ComCat ML anchors among its near events (dominated: anchors with at least half of their picks on the group); stiffness k = misfit increase per delta^2 when all its terms move by +delta and the events are re-fitted (the Schur complement; equal to the sum over events of n_G n_other / n, an effective number of tie picks); se_level = formal standard error of the mean term of the group minus the mean land term (sigma = 0.245, from the full inverse of the reduced system); dphi_opt_0.5 and dphi_naive_0.5 = misfit increase for delta = 0.5 with the events re-fitted, and with every event that has a pick on the group moved by -delta (the +delta/-delta test; total misfit 72,319); dC_minus_land = change of the mean term (converged minus stored) relative to the land mean; dML_dominated = median ML change of the events with at least half of their picks on the group; anchor_gap = median ML - ComCat ML of the dominated anchors.

Source of the 'before' columns (dC_minus_land, dML_dominated, anchor_gap_unconv): for v4.1, a legacy3000 rerun at 12 threads, because the stored run did not keep its per-pick table. anchor_gap_stored_file uses the stored v4.1 file itself. For v5.1, the stored v5.1 run.

Uncertainty of the levels. The formal s.e. assumes independent Gaussian residuals and a correct model. The verifier's bootstrap (32 replicates, resampling events) gives errors 1.0-1.7 times the formal ones (7D Y2 0.016 vs 0.010, X9 0.023 vs 0.016, NV 2014 0.12 vs 0.085). A model test shifts the thinly tied levels by about 0.1: with picks within 100 km instead of 150 km, Axial -0.15, Explorer +0.13, Endeavour -0.11. Blanco, Gorda and Mendocino move by -0.04 to +0.04 in that test. The NC terms sit 0.19 below the other land networks (bootstrap s.d. 0.014).

What the table shows:

  • No deployment is free. The largest formal error of a deployment level is 0.085-0.091 (NV 2014, bootstrap 0.12, 4 terms, 2 or fewer events with land picks); every other is 0.009-0.046 (bootstrap 0.011-0.051). A 0.5 shift of a deployment costs from 2 (NV 2014) to 6,900 (7D Y4) in misfit, out of about 72,000.
  • Thin ties (stiffness below about 400): NV 2014 (k 8-10), 7A 2010 (69-75), NV 2011 (117-119; 0-2 events with land picks), OO 2014 (194-200; 66-71 of its 22,000 events have land picks), NV 2010 (244-256), NV 2013 (360-367) and 7D Y1 (376-406). Their levels rest on few links. OO 2014 carries the Axial catalog.
  • X9 2012 (Blanco) has only 3-4 events with land picks. It is tied through 3,800 events shared with 7D Y2, 401 with 7D Y3 and 108 with Z5 2013 (stiffness 5,300, s.e. 0.016); 7D Y2 in turn shares 2,615 events with land. It moved most (-0.67 to -0.71) because LSQR reaches this chain last, not because the data leave it free.
  • Anchors versus cross-links. In phase19 the 3,416 anchors (84% onshore) set one global offset and do not enter the deployment levels; the cross-links set every level. The anchors are an independent check. Where a deployment has 9 or more dominated anchors, convergence reduces the gap. Against the stored v4.1 file: 7D Y2 +0.32 -> +0.03 (24 anchors), 7D Y4 +0.20 -> +0.02 (43), Z5 2013 +0.25 -> -0.09 (38), X9 +0.89 -> +0.23 (9). The 12-thread legacy rerun gives +0.30, +0.17, +0.22, +0.87. Z5 2014 gets worse: -0.06 in the stored file (-0.12 in the rerun) -> -0.13 (13 anchors). OO 2014 (Axial) stays at +0.39/+0.40 with only 4 anchors; the 2 anchors in the Axial region are +0.9 above ComCat in both solutions. Axial is the one place where the anchors disagree with the cross-link level, and its ties are thin (open problem 1).
  • The land network is not one rigid block either. The northern California network NC (128 terms) moves by +0.15 (v4.1) and +0.25 (v5.1) against the other land networks, and BK by +0.10/+0.17. Events dominated by NC change by -0.17/-0.29. This is why Mendocino, Gorda and the offshore forearc change by the same -0.19 (v4.1) in every year, 2010 and 2011 included, when no ocean-bottom station was recording. NC is stiffly tied (s.e. 0.010; 21,030 events shared with the other land networks), so this too was the solver. Its 54 dominated anchors go from +0.39 to +0.24 above ComCat ML; the remaining +0.24 may be a scale difference between the NC local magnitudes in ComCat and the PNSN ones that dominate the anchor offset.

The tensor comparison is inconclusive. For near events at offshore labels with Mw 3-4.5 (43 events), ML - Mw goes from +0.11 [-0.05, +0.20] to -0.07 [-0.21, +0.02] (v4.1; median and bootstrap 95% interval) and from +0.26 [+0.07, +0.28] to -0.02 [-0.21, +0.03] (v5.1). The intervals overlap, and by region Gorda gets worse (-0.03 -> -0.22, 10 events) while Mendocino and the offshore forearc get better. The tensors do not reject either solution; the ComCat ML anchors (549 offshore and coastal, 3,416 in all) are the stronger test. Onshore, ML - Mw stays at +0.05 to +0.12. Counted over all events, the offshore value goes to -0.21/-0.23 because of the 11-14 'mapped' tensor events: their ML comes from the Theil-Sen map of the inversion ML, whose slope fell from 1.15 to 1.01 when the near ML it is fitted to came down. phase19 already flags mapped ML above about 4 as lower bounds. Above Mw 4.5 the tensor Mw is used, so these values do not enter M.

D-B091 on the stored pick sets

These comparisons use the stored system (stored pick set, isolated term included, two gauge rows), which is what the stored runs and the D-B091 check solved; its exact solution gives the same ML as the new one-row system (column max_abs_dML_exact_new_vs_stored_system). On the pick set of the stored v5.1 run, the exact solver reproduces the D-B091 changes, and the D-B091 LSQR to istop 2 (4,863 iterations) is within 0.006 of it in every region except Axial (-0.03); its largest event error is 0.18. On the v4.1 pick set (the stored per-pick table was not kept, so a 12-thread legacy rerun stands in) the same LSQR is within 0.02 except Axial (+0.06). The data misfit drops by 274 (v5.1, 0.38%) and 184 (v4.1, 0.25%) from the stored to the exact solution. Redoing the first pass and the 4-MAD rejection with the exact solver changes only tens of picks per deployment and the regional medians by at most 0.02 (columns full_chain_minus_stored and rejection_effect). The larger Explorer and Endeavour changes in the all-event region tables come from the 'mapped' events (Explorer: 485 of 1,326), not from the rejection.

Same estimators, grid and boxes as the v5.1 magnitude piece (workflow/06_analysis/v51_mc_b.py, which imports v4_mc_maps.py: MAXC+0.2, MBS, GFT90/95, the Woessner & Wiemer best rule, 200 bootstrap resamples, Aki-Utsu b with the Shi & Bolt error). Offshore Mc drops by 0.2-0.6 with the magnitudes. With the paper's script (v4_mc_maps.py, mc_maps_v41/mc_regional.csv): Blanco 2.2 -> 1.6, Gorda 2.1 -> 1.9, Mendocino triple junction 1.7 -> 1.5, Endeavour-Explorer 1.8 -> 1.6, offshore pooled 2.2 -> 1.7. The Gorda value is borderline: GFT95 is reached at 1.9 there, but not in version A of v51_mc_b.py (the same events plus 3 duplicated rows of 900001-900003), which falls back to GFT90 = 1.7 with b 1.05 instead of 1.22. Onshore Mc does not change. Two period statements of the paper change. The Blanco Mc of 2011-2012 (2.6 stored) was inflated by the same deployment levels: converged it is 1.5, against 1.6 in 2013-2015, so the 'offshore Mc improved by 0.2-0.4 after the first two years' result does not hold (EN +0.1, BL -0.1, GO 0.0). The rate of M >= 2.5 Blanco events in 2010 and 2016, relative to 2013-2015, rises from 5% and 8% to 28% and 29%: the events of the ocean-bottom years came down by 0.6-0.7, those of 2010 and 2016 (mapped, land stations only) by about 0.3. The Mendocino 2016 ratio stays at 10-11%. b changes by -0.07 to +0.12 in the offshore boxes. In the onshore box (everything outside the named boxes) b goes from 0.92 to 1.01 although its median ML change is +0.01: 11% of its events drop by more than 0.1, half of them in northern California between 40 and 42 N (east of the triple-junction box, recorded by the Gorda and Mendocino ocean-bottom stations) and 12% of them 'mapped' events. Between converged v5.1 and converged v4.1 M (paired test, same events) b agrees within 0.03 in every box except Axial (+0.10 at Mc 0.1, the Axial relocation).

8. Files, reproduction, open problems

Code (branch analysis/mag-converged): workflow/05_magnitude/phase19_solver.py (new), phase19_preferred_magnitude.py (solver, --solver/--outdir/--tag, provenance), v51_magnitude_table.py (--pm/--out/--tag/--solver/--v4-mags), mag_converged.py (patch, near, threads, gauge, compare, reconcile, mcb), mag_converged_report.py and mag_converged_text.py (this page), scale/run_magnitude_converged.sh (driver). Resume notes: /wd1/mdenolle_data/magnitude_converged/RESUME.md.

Open problems

  1. Axial (OO 2014): converged ML is still +0.39 above ComCat ML on its 4 dominated anchors and +0.9 on the 2 anchors of the Axial region. The OO level rests on 66-71 events with land picks (stiffness about 200). Its level should be checked against the OOI/PNSN Axial catalogs before the Axial magnitudes are used for b or Mc.
  2. JdF ridge/plate and the 7D Y1/Y3 J stations: v4.1 near events move by -0.29 and v5.1 by -0.51, because the two stored runs stopped at different points; both converged runs agree (v5.1 - v4.1 = +0.005). The JdF plate has 4 ComCat anchors in total, so its level rests on the cross-links (7D Y1 stiffness about 400, s.e. 0.03) with no external check.
  3. Model uncertainty of the thinly tied levels: the 100 km pick-selection test moves Axial by -0.15, Explorer by +0.13 and Endeavour by -0.11 (verifier). These regions carry about 0.1 of uncertainty beyond the formal errors.
  4. 'Mapped' events (3,522 in v4.1) follow the Theil-Sen map fitted to the near events; the map changed (slope 1.15 -> 1.01), so mapped ML above about 3.5 dropped more than the region shift. Their tensor comparison (ML - Mw about -0.2 at Mw 3-4.5) is worse than before.
  5. The near-event Mw_cal offset rose from +0.04 to +0.19 (v4.1) because large offshore ML dropped while the tensors did not change; Mw_cal events: 35 -> 27. The ML - Mw shortfall above Mw 4.5 is larger (-0.79 -> -1.15 for all, -0.36 -> -0.69 for near events), which strengthens the case for the Mw switch.
  6. The converged v4.1 file is not placed next to the stored one in the main tree (other worktrees are not touched); the clustering rerun has no sensitivity variants; the paper figures 1, 3, 5, 6 and the atlas are not remade.
